rows.jp: 桜庭に押し倒される夢を見た。
rows.en: I dreamed Sakuraba had pinned me to the ground.

ghs.en: I dreamed of Sakuraba pushing himself on me.

rows.jp: 『男でもいい』

ghs.en: Sakuraba: 『A MAN IS FINE TOO!』

rows.jp: と叫びつつ、襲いかかる金髪の貴公子。
rows.en: The blond nobleman yelled this as he lunged at me.

ghs.en: So shouts the gold-haired noble young man that's swooping down on me.

rows.jp: しかしそれはおかしいじゃないか。

ghs.en: Wait, isn't that weird?

rows.jp: 当時、やつは金髪ではなかったのだから。
rows.en: His hair hadn’t been blond back then.

ghs.en: Because at that time the guy wasn't blond.

rows.jp: でもどうでもいいことだ。

ghs.en: But that's just whatever.

rows.jp: 最強の矛と無敵の楯を装備している桜庭は、もとより理屈の通じない相手だ。
rows.en: Armed with both the strongest spear and the invincible shield, Sakuraba was immune to reason from the start.

ghs.en: Sakuraba is equipped with a lance that can pierce any shield and a shield that can stop any lance, so from the very start he was never an opponent that could be reached through reason.

rows.jp: 『避妊するから』

ghs.en: Sakuraba: 『IT'S CONTRACEPTIVE!』
ghs.assessment: The speaker promises to use contraception or protection. The English instead applies the adjective 'contraceptive' to an unspecified thing and loses the promised action.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I'll use protection.'

rows.jp: と言い訳がましく迫りくる。
rows.en: He closed in with that feeble excuse.

ghs.en: That's the justification-like thing he tells me as he approaches.

rows.jp: 避妊すると言いつつ肉体関係を強要してくる、桜庭自体を否認したかった。
rows.en: He claimed he’d use protection while forcing sex on me; I wanted protection from Sakuraba’s very existence.

ghs.en: If Sakuraba was going to force carnal relationships while saying it's contraceptive, then I wanted to reject him from the very body.
ghs.assessment: The narrator wants to deny or reject Sakuraba himself for forcing a sexual relationship under that pretext. The English misparses 'himself' as a phrase about rejecting him from a body.
ghs.remedy: Say that he wanted to deny Sakuraba's very existence or reject Sakuraba himself.

highlights.text: reject him from the very body

rows.jp: どうしてこんなことに？
rows.en: How had it come to this?

ghs.en: Why is this happening to me?

rows.jp: 日記にひどいことを書いたせいか？
rows.en: Was this because of the awful things I’d written in my diary?

ghs.en: Are the mean things I wrote in my diary?
ghs.assessment: The source asks whether this is happening because of the cruel things he wrote. The English drops the causal predicate and leaves an incomplete question about the things themselves.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Is it because of the mean things I wrote in my diary?'

highlights.text: Are the mean things I wrote in my diary?

rows.jp: 天罰か？

ghs.en: Wrath of God?

rows.jp: 応報か？

ghs.en: Just recompense?

rows.jp: ハンムラビ法典か？

ghs.en: The Code of Hammurabi?

rows.jp: そりゃ微妙に違うか？
rows.en: That last one wasn’t quite right, was it?

ghs.en: Aren't they only slightly different?
ghs.assessment: The source singles out the immediately preceding comparison as perhaps slightly off. The English instead compares the whole plural set to one another and reverses the tentative self-correction.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Maybe that one's a little different?'

rows.jp: 俺はと言うと、どこかで夢だと知りつつも、パニック状態になっていた。
rows.en: Some part of me knew it was a dream, but I was panicking all the same.

ghs.en: Whatever it may be, while I still know it's a dream that came from somewhere, I still slip into panic mode.
ghs.assessment: He knows at some level that this is a dream but panics anyway. The English attaches 'somewhere' to the dream's origin, inventing a provenance instead of locating his awareness.
ghs.remedy: Use 'though somewhere in my mind I knew it was a dream.'

highlights.text: a dream that came from somewhere

rows.jp: 『からだはいやーっ』

ghs.en: Taichi: 『My body, you caaan't!』

rows.jp: 『お慈悲！』

ghs.en: Taichi: 『Have mercy!』

rows.jp: 『けだもの～っ！』

ghs.en: Taichi: 『Animaaa～l!』

rows.jp: などと叫びながら、桜庭の体を突き飛ばそうとする。
rows.en: Shouting all this, I tried to shove Sakuraba off me.

ghs.en: And all that sort of shouts I make while I try to thrust Sakuraba's body away.

rows.jp: 純潔をかけたレスリング。

ghs.en: A wrestling match with my chastity at stake.

rows.jp: ……純潔でもないが。

ghs.en: ...not that I'm chaste.

rows.jp: 敵は本気で、鼻息も荒い。
rows.en: My opponent was serious, breathing hard.

ghs.en: My opponent is serious, so wildly snorting in excitement.

rows.jp: 殺すかと本気で思う。

ghs.en: There's some serious thoughts of murder here.

rows.jp: ぼかぼかと殴る。

ghs.en: Strikes that go thunk, thunk.

rows.jp: 一発がうまくクリーンヒット。

ghs.en: One of them is a skillful clean hit.
ghs.assessment: One blow successfully lands as a clean hit. The English turns the adverb of successful contact into a claim that the hit itself is skillful.
ghs.remedy: Use 'One of them lands cleanly.'

rows.jp: 桜庭は横転する。

ghs.en: Sakuraba flips over.

rows.jp: 仰臥(ぎょうが)して意識を失った桜庭の股間が、不意に暴発した。
rows.en: As he lay unconscious on his back, Sakuraba’s crotch suddenly went off.

ghs.en: Supine, his sense lost, Sakuraba's nethers unconsciously discharged.
ghs.assessment: The discharge happens suddenly or unexpectedly after he loses consciousness. 'Unconsciously' changes the adverb into a claim about the manner or agency of the discharge.
ghs.remedy: Use 'suddenly discharged' or 'unexpectedly went off.'

rows.jp: 射精したのかと思ったら、桜庭の荷電粒子砲（自称）の先端からは、手品さながらに花束が突きだしていた。
rows.en: I thought he had ejaculated, but instead a bouquet shot from the tip of Sakuraba’s self-proclaimed charged-particle cannon like a magic trick.

ghs.en: While I thought whether he'd ejaculate, from the pointed tip of Sakuraba's Charged Particle Cannon (self-named) out blows a bundle of flowers, as in a magician's trick.
ghs.assessment: The narrator first thinks he has ejaculated, only for flowers to emerge. The English makes this a simultaneous question about a future ejaculation and loses the reveal structure.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Just when I thought he'd ejaculated...'

highlights.text: While I thought whether he'd ejaculate

rows.jp: ああ。

ghs.en: Aw.

rows.jp: なんて悪趣味な展開なんだ。
rows.en: What an appallingly tasteless turn of events.

ghs.en: What a development in bad taste.

rows.jp: 目を覆う。

ghs.en: I cover my eyes.

rows.jp: そこで目が覚めた。

ghs.en: And that was when I was awake.

rows.jp: 「……シュールすぎる」

ghs.en: Taichi: "...way too surreal."

rows.jp: だいたいあいつに、人を押し倒す度胸なんてあるはずないのだ。
rows.en: Besides, he didn’t have the nerve to pin anyone down.

ghs.en: Besides, I wouldn't expect that guy to have the pluck to push himself on somebody.

rows.jp: 気弱なお坊ちゃんなのだ。
rows.en: He was a timid little rich boy.

ghs.en: He's a fainthearted obou-chan.
ghs.assessment: The honorific noun characterizes him as a sheltered or pampered young master. Leaving it as an unexplained romanization with an English suffix untranslated withholds that characterization.
ghs.remedy: Use 'a fainthearted, sheltered young master' or an equivalent characterization.

rows.jp: どうせなら見里先輩に逆レイプされる夢ならよかったのに。
rows.en: If I had to dream about being raped, why couldn’t it have been Misato instead?

ghs.en: But if I have to have one, I wish it was a dream where I'm reverse-raped by Misato-senpai.

rows.jp: 『……こんなに大きくなってしまう悪いお肉には、この鞭でたっぷりとおしおきしなければいけませんね！』
rows.en: “...This naughty piece of meat has grown so big, I’ll have to punish it thoroughly with my whip!”

ghs.en: Misato 『...this nasty little meat has gotten so very big, that I cannot but punish it most thoroughly with this whip!』

rows.jp: 素敵すぎる……。

ghs.en: Way too awesome...

rows.jp: うっとりしながら着替えた。
rows.en: I got dressed in a dreamy haze.

ghs.en: I change my clothes while still spellbound.

rows.jp: 朝食が用意してある。

ghs.en: Breakfast had been prepared,

rows.jp: メモもあった。

ghs.en: and there was also a note.

rows.jp: 『しっかり食べて行ってらっしゃい』
rows.en: “Eat a good breakfast. Have a good day.”

ghs.en: 『Eat properly and have a nice day』

rows.jp: 美人でキャリアな睦美おばさんは、料理もうまい。
rows.en: Beautiful, successful Aunt Mutsumi was a good cook too.

ghs.en: Beautiful career woman Mutsumi-obasan is also good at cooking.

rows.jp: 忙しくて家にはほとんどいないけど。
rows.en: She was so busy she was almost never home, though.

ghs.en: She's so busy that she's almost never home, though.

rows.jp: 頭が下がる。
rows.en: I had nothing but respect for her.

ghs.en: I bow my head to that.
ghs.assessment: The idiom expresses admiration, respect, or feeling humbled by her effort. The English literalizes it as a physical bow and loses the evaluative meaning.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I have to admire her' or 'I'm humbled.'

highlights.text: I bow my head to that.

rows.jp: お言葉に甘えて、分厚いサンドイッチを野菜ジュースで流し込んだ。
rows.en: Taking her up on it, I washed down a thick sandwich with vegetable juice.

ghs.en: Presuming upon her kind offer, I wash down a thick sandwich with some vegetable juice.

rows.jp: 時間がない。

ghs.en: I don't have time.

rows.jp: 残りはラップに包んでポケットに入れた。
rows.en: I wrapped the rest in plastic and put it in my pocket.

ghs.en: I pack back the leftovers in the wrapping and put them into my pocket.

rows.jp: 途中で食べていこう。
rows.en: I’d eat it on the way.

ghs.en: I'll eat on the way.

rows.jp: さんさんと自己主張する日差し。
rows.en: The blazing sunlight made its presence aggressively known.

ghs.en: The rays of the sun assert themselves with brilliance.

rows.jp: 朝からこれだ。
rows.en: And this early in the morning.

ghs.en: This starts all the way from morning.

rows.jp: 気が滅入る。

ghs.en: I feel depressed.

rows.jp: しばらく歩いていると、
rows.en: After I had walked a while—

ghs.en: And after I've been walking for a while,

rows.jp: 「あぎゃらおーーーーーーーーっ！！」

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "Ah'gyarooooooooow!!!"

rows.jp: 桜庭の悲鳴だ。

ghs.en: That's Sakuraba's scream.

rows.jp: わりと近い。

ghs.en: It's relatively near.

rows.jp: 犬の吠え声と、悲鳴がさらに重なる。
rows.en: A dog’s barking joined the screams.

ghs.en: The howl of a dog further overlaps the scream.

rows.jp: 遠ざかっていく。

ghs.en: And then they fade away.

rows.jp: 「なるほど……」

ghs.en: Taichi: "I get it..."

rows.jp: 得心した。

ghs.en: I was satisfied.
ghs.assessment: The verb means that he understood or was convinced by what he inferred. 'Satisfied' substitutes contentment for comprehension.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I understood' or 'That convinced me.'

rows.jp: と、そこに―――

ghs.en: Then, right there---

rows.jp: 「はれ？　太一さん？」

ghs.en: Girl: "Oh my? Taichi-san?"

rows.jp: 「おはよう」

ghs.en: Taichi: "'Morning."

rows.jp: 「あ、おはようですっ」

ghs.en: Girl: "Ah, good morning, yes!"

rows.jp: ぺこりと頭を下げる。

ghs.en: She bows her head with a sharp bob.

rows.jp: 近所に住む美少女の遊紗ちゃん。
rows.en: Yusa, the beautiful girl who lived nearby.

ghs.en: This is Yusa-chan, the beautiful young girl that leaves near me.
ghs.assessment: The line identifies a beautiful girl who lives nearby. The English uses 'leaves' instead of 'lives,' reversing the residence verb through a mechanical word error.
ghs.remedy: Replace 'leaves' with 'lives.'

rows.jp: 上見坂いい街。

ghs.en: Nice town Kamisaka.

rows.jp: 説明不要なほど可愛い遊紗ちゃんの、両手にカレーパンが揺れていた。
rows.en: Yusa’s cuteness spoke for itself. A curry bun bobbed in each hand.

ghs.en: Yusa-chan, so cute it doesn't require exposition, held a loaf of curry bread swaying in her hands.

rows.jp: 二人で並んで歩き出す。
rows.en: We set off side by side.

ghs.en: The two of us line up and set out to walk.

rows.jp: 別に今日にはじまったことでもない。
rows.en: Not that this was anything new.

ghs.en: It's not really something that began today,

rows.jp: なにせ同じ学校に向かうのだから。
rows.en: We were headed to the same school, after all.

ghs.en: it's because the two of us are going towards the same school anyway.

rows.jp: 後ろから、『い゛っでら゛っしゃーい！！』というハスキーな声が聞こえた。
rows.en: Behind us came a husky “Haaave a gooood daaaay!”

ghs.en: From behind us I could hear a 『Habe a nice daaaaaaaay!』 in a husky voice.

rows.jp: 遊紗ちゃんの母君だ。

ghs.en: That is Yusa-chan's mother.

rows.jp: ちょっと重くていらっしゃる。
rows.en: She was on the heavy side.

ghs.en: She's sort on the heavy side,
ghs.assessment: The intended euphemism that she is sort of on the heavy side is clear, but the missing 'of' creates a mechanical grammar error.
ghs.remedy: Use 'sort of on the heavy side.'

rows.jp: が、毎日楽しそうに生きておられるから、よしとしよう。
rows.en: But she seemed to enjoy life every day, so good for her.

ghs.en: but it's all fine, since she lets me have something enjoyable every day.
ghs.assessment: The mother herself appears to live happily every day, which the narrator takes as sufficient. The English instead claims she provides him with daily enjoyment, changing the subject and inventing a benefit to him.
ghs.remedy: Say that she seems to enjoy life every day, so he will call it fine.

highlights.text: she lets me have something enjoyable every day

rows.jp: 平凡な家庭に生まれた美少女。
rows.en: A beautiful girl born into an ordinary family.

ghs.en: A beautiful girl that was born to a family this mediocre...

rows.jp: ただ一つ難点があるとすれば、世間を知らなすぎること。
rows.en: Her one flaw was knowing far too little of the world.

ghs.en: If I had to find a just one blemish in her, it'd be that she is completely clueless of all things worldly.
ghs.assessment: The duplicated determiner and adverb make a mechanical grammar error in an otherwise accurate statement that her one flaw is excessive naivety.
ghs.remedy: Use 'just one blemish' or 'a single blemish.'

rows.jp: そんな遊紗ちゃんの、異性の先輩として一番身近な俺に課せられた責任は小さくない。
rows.en: As the older boy she knew best, I bore no small responsibility.

ghs.en: As the most familiar Senpai of opposite sex to little Yusa-chan, the responsibility given me is no little thing.

rows.jp: 「いってきまーす！」

ghs.en: Yusa: "I am going ooout!"

rows.jp: 手を振り返す、その顔に反抗期の陰もなく。
rows.en: She waved back, not a trace of adolescent rebellion on her face.

ghs.en: She returns a wave of the hand, on her face not a shadow of that rebellious age.

rows.jp: どころか、第一次性徴さえまだなのではないかと思われる節もある。
rows.en: Indeed, there were signs she hadn’t even entered puberty yet.

ghs.en: Far from it, as it appears we're also at a time where even her primary sexual characteristics might not be there yet.

rows.jp: この真っ白なキャンバスを俺色に染めあげたいと思ってしまうのは男として至極当然のことだが中等コースの一年で身長は前から三番目で――
rows.en: Of course any man would want to dye this blank canvas in his own colors—but she was only a first-year in the junior division, third-shortest in her class, and—

rows.jp: 憶えたての敬語がたどたどしくも初々しい遊紗ちゃんの純正は宝石にも増して煌びやかで我が妄想も汚すか否かの瀬戸際で――
rows.en: her halting, newly learned polite speech was still so fresh, her innocence more radiant than any jewel, while my imagination trembled at the brink of defiling it—and—

rows.jp: いつも切なげかつ悩ましげに揺れているのであるがその反復思考自体すでにペド狂人のものであるという自覚はある。あるんだってば。
rows.en: kept wavering there, wistful and fevered, although I knew the very recurrence of such thoughts marked me as a pedophilic madman. I knew. I’m telling you, I knew.

rows.jp: ま、とにかく揺れているのだ。
rows.en: Anyway, the point was that something was swaying.

ghs.en: Well, for now they're swaying.

rows.jp: そう、遊紗ちゃんが手に持つカレーパンの袋のように。
rows.en: Yes. Like the curry-bun bags in Yusa’s hands.

ghs.en: Yes, just like that bag of curry bread that Yusa-chan has in her hands.

rows.jp: 「カレーパンだね」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Isn't that curry bread?"

rows.jp: 「です」

ghs.en: Yusa: "It is!"

rows.jp: 歩くたびに前後にゆらゆら揺れる。
rows.en: They swayed back and forth as she walked.

ghs.en: With each step a sway, back and forth, back and forth.

rows.jp: 両手を幽霊みたいに掲げて、誇示するかのように進む。
rows.en: She marched with both hands raised like a ghost, as though putting them on display.

ghs.en: As if being cradled by a ghost, the sway nothing but a manifestation of its existence.
ghs.assessment: She walks with both hands raised like a ghost, as if displaying the item. The English invents a ghost cradling something, changes the subject to the sway, and omits her pose and forward motion.
ghs.remedy: Say that she walks on with both hands raised like a ghost, as though showing it off.

highlights.text: As if being cradled by a ghost, the sway nothing but a manifestation of its existence.

rows.jp: 「それは……朝食？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Is that... breakfast?"

rows.jp: 「あの、さっきそこに桜庭さんがいて」

ghs.en: Yusa: "Uhm, Sakuraba-san was there earlier."

rows.jp: 「うん、いたね」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Yep, was is the word."
ghs.assessment: The answer confirms that he was there, but the English retains two competing copulas and is mechanically ungrammatical.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Yep, he was.'

rows.jp: 「会いましたか？」

ghs.en: Yusa: "Did you meet him?"

rows.jp: 「いや、形跡があった」

ghs.en: Taichi: "No, there was some evidence left."

rows.jp: 「けいせき？」

ghs.en: Yusa: "Evidence?"

rows.jp: 「ま、俺が来たときにはいなかったけど」
rows.en: “Well, he was gone by the time I arrived.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Well, by the time I came around he wasn't among us anymore."

rows.jp: 「困っちゃいました」

ghs.en: Yusa: "Oh, what a problem."

rows.jp: 「カレーパンあげようと思ったのですけど」
rows.en: “I was going to give him a curry bun.”

ghs.en: Yusa: "I thought I would give him this curry bread."

rows.jp: 餌付けしようとしてたらしい。
rows.en: Apparently she had been trying to feed him like a stray.

ghs.en: Seems like she was going to feed the wild animal to train it to human contact.

rows.jp: 「あいつ、コンバットに嫌われてるからさ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "It's because Combat hates that guy."

rows.jp: 「吉田さんちの猛犬コンバットですね」
rows.en: “Combat, the ferocious dog from the Yoshidas’ house.”

ghs.en: Yusa: "That ferocious dog Combat, at Yoshida-san's house?"

rows.jp: 「やつは凄いぞ。自力で鎖の繋がった楔を引き抜くことができる」
rows.en: “He’s amazing. He can pull the stake anchoring his chain out of the ground by himself.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "That guy's awesome. He can uproot the wedge where his chain is fastened on his own."

rows.jp: 「外出したい時に出ていき、戻りたい時に戻るのだ」
rows.en: “He leaves whenever he wants and comes back whenever he wants.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "When that guy wants to leave he leaves, when he wants to return he returns."

rows.jp: 「コンバットは一般のひとは攻撃しませんよ」

ghs.en: Yusa: "But Combat doesn't normally attack people!"
ghs.assessment: The dog does not attack ordinary members of the public. The English instead says it does not normally attack people, changing a restriction on targets into a frequency claim.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Combat doesn't attack ordinary people.'

rows.jp: 「本物の極道ってのはそういうものさ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "And a true gangster is exactly that sort."

rows.jp: 「ごくどう……だったのか……」

ghs.en: Yusa: "True... gangster...?"

rows.jp: 「今は恰幅が良くなってしまったが、奴には軍人の血が流れてるからな」
rows.en: “He’s put on weight now, but the blood of a soldier still runs in his veins.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Today his physique has improved, but the blood of soldiers flows inside that guy."
ghs.assessment: The dog has now grown stout or portly, not improved its physique. The English reverses the bodily change into a positive fitness claim.
ghs.remedy: Use 'He's grown stout now, but...'

rows.jp: 「人間で言えば、戦争帰りの古き良き親分といったところか」
rows.en: “In human terms, he’s a good old-fashioned boss back from the war.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "To put it in human terms, I'd say he's sort of like a good ol' criminal boss having returned home from the war."

rows.jp: 「しかし桜庭にだけは攻撃をする」
rows.en: “But Sakuraba is the only one he attacks.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Yet he only ever attacks Sakuraba."

rows.jp: 「不思議です」

ghs.en: Yusa: "That's inexplicable."

rows.jp: 「不思議だねぇ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Inexplicable it is."

rows.jp: ゆったりとしたペースで歩く。
rows.en: We walked at an easy pace.

ghs.en: We walk at a leisurely pace.

rows.jp: 「これどうしたら……」

ghs.en: Yusa: "What will I do with this..."

rows.jp: 「おなか、すいてますか？」

ghs.en: Yusa: "Would you be hungry, maybe?"

rows.jp: 「一個ずつ食べようか？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Wanna eat half each?"
ghs.assessment: He suggests eating one item each. The English instead divides a single item into halves, changing the quantity and action.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Want to eat one each?'

rows.jp: 「はい」

ghs.en: Yusa: "Yes!"

rows.jp: 二人でカレーパンを食べた。
rows.en: We ate the curry buns together.

ghs.en: The two of us ate the curry bread.

rows.jp: 「ガッコー慣れた？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "You fitting in at school?"

rows.jp: 「まだちょっと」

ghs.en: Yusa: "Well, a bit."

rows.jp: 「いじめは？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Bullying?"

rows.jp: 「全然ないんです！　よかったですー！」

ghs.en: Yusa: "None there is none! I'm so lucky!"
ghs.assessment: The first clause correctly intends that there is none at all, but duplicates incompatible constructions and is mechanically ungrammatical.
ghs.remedy: Use 'There's none at all!'

rows.jp: 「だろうねぇ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ain't that nice."
ghs.assessment: The reply conveys 'I thought so' or 'I figured,' confirming an expectation. The English changes this into a positive evaluation that the situation is nice.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Thought so' or 'I figured.'

rows.jp: それから鼻汁橋を回収しつつ、自分の制服を軽く拭いた。
rows.en: Then I gathered up the snot bridge and gave my uniform a quick wipe.

ghs.en: After that comes the collection of the snot bridge while very carefully wiping down my own uniform.

rows.jp: ハンカチをポケットに戻す。戻そうとする。
rows.en: I put the handkerchief back in my pocket. Tried to.

ghs.en: I return the hanky to pocket. And as I try,

rows.jp: 「あ、だめ、だめですよっ！？」

ghs.en: Yusa: "Ah, you can't, you can't do that!"

rows.jp: 「んー？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Hmm?"

rows.jp: 「そんなききき汚いっ、あ、それはだめ、捨てないと、あ、あのっ」
rows.en: “It’s d-d-dirty! No, you can’t—you have to throw it away, um—”

ghs.en: Yusa: "It's di-di-di-dirty, ah, you can't, must throw it away, ah, uhm!"

rows.jp: 「べんしょーしますっ！」

ghs.en: Yusa: "I'll reimburse it!"

rows.jp: 「いいんだよ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "It's fine."

rows.jp: 朗らかに笑って。

ghs.en: So I say with a bright smile.

rows.jp: 「さ、行こうか」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Well, shall we go?"

rows.jp: 「だから、その、ごめんなさっ、でもハンカチっ」
rows.en: “But, um, I’m so sorry, and the handkerchief—”

ghs.en: Yusa: "But I said, that's, so sorry, your handkerchief!"

rows.jp: 今度こそ、親指の腹で涙をぬぐいつつ。
rows.en: This time, I wiped her tears with the pad of my thumb.

ghs.en: This time I can indeed wipe her tears with the belly of my thumbs.
ghs.assessment: He wipes the tears with the pad of one thumb. The English changes the singular body part to both thumbs.
ghs.remedy: Use 'the pad of my thumb.'

rows.jp: 「可愛い後輩を、困らせたままにしておくようなハンカチじゃないんだよ」
rows.en: “No handkerchief is worth leaving a sweet younger student in distress.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Leaving a cute Kouhai in trouble is not worth a handkerchief."
ghs.assessment: He says this is not a handkerchief that would leave a cute junior in distress, valuing her welfare above the cloth. The English reverses the relation and says leaving her in trouble is not worth a handkerchief.
ghs.remedy: Use 'This isn't a handkerchief worth leaving a cute junior in trouble over.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Leaving a cute Kouhai in trouble is not worth a handkerchief."

rows.jp: 少女は大きなショックを受けた。

ghs.en: That struck her greatly.

rows.jp: 「弁償はいいけど、風邪には気をつけた方がいいな、遊紗君」
rows.en: “Forget paying me back. Just be careful not to catch cold, Yusa.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Reimburse is no problem, but you'd better watch out for colds, Yusa-kun."
ghs.assessment: He says compensation is unnecessary, then warns her about catching cold. The English instead suggests reimbursement is acceptable or unproblematic and is also grammatically malformed.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Don't worry about replacing it, but...'

rows.jp: ぽん、と頭を軽く叩いて、歩き出す。
rows.en: I gave her a light pat on the head and walked on.

ghs.en: Tok, I gently give her a light poke on the face, and resume walking.
ghs.assessment: He gives her head a light pat or tap before walking on. The English moves the contact to her face and changes it into a poke.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I lightly pat her on the head.'

rows.jp: 遊紗ちゃんは、茫然としていた。

ghs.en: Yusa-chan stood dumbfounded.

rows.jp: 「ヘイ、学校だ、お嬢さん」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Hey, to school, ojou-san!"

rows.jp: 「はいっ」

ghs.en: Yusa: "Yes!"

rows.jp: 小走りで駆けてきて、

ghs.en: She comes over at half run.
Yusa: "..."
Taichi: "Hm?"

rows.jp: 手を握ってきた。

ghs.en: She grabbed my hand.

rows.jp: 耳までまっ赤にして、俯いたまま。

ghs.en: Her face is cast downwards, vivid red up to her ears.

rows.jp: 可愛いもんだ。あれだけのことで。
rows.en: She was adorable, getting that worked up over so little.

ghs.en: So damn adorable. Just because of that little thing!

rows.jp: ハンカチ一枚で射止められた少女の好意を、べつだん安いとは思わなかった。
rows.en: I didn’t think her affection cheap merely because a single handkerchief had won it.

ghs.en: I didn't think the the goodwill of this girl that I made all mine with a single handkerchief to be particularly cheap,
ghs.assessment: The duplicated article is a mechanical grammar error in an otherwise recoverable judgment about the girl's goodwill.
ghs.remedy: Remove one occurrence of 'the.'

rows.jp: だが同時に彼女におもいっきり子供生ませたいと思ってしまった俺は脳が腐っていること間違いなかった。死ね、死んでしまえ。
rows.en: Yet at the very same time I desperately wanted to make her bear my children, which left no doubt my brain was rotten. Die. Just die.

ghs.en: but simultaneously wanting for this girl to birth me a baby with all her heart meant my brain was rotten, and no mistake. Die, just die.
ghs.assessment: The narrator intensely wants to make the girl bear his children. The English attaches the intensity to how wholeheartedly she would bear a baby, changing whose desire is being described.
ghs.remedy: Attach the intensity to his desire rather than to her imagined action.

rows.jp: 冬子がいた。

ghs.en: Touko was here.

rows.jp: というか、いっつも一等賞じゃないか、こいつ。
rows.en: Or rather, didn’t she always win first prize for getting here early?

ghs.en: Or should I say, alllways shooting for first place, ain't she.
ghs.assessment: He remarks that she is always the first-place arrival, not that she is continually aspiring or trying to win first place. The English turns an observed result into intention.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She's always first place, isn't she?'

rows.jp: 「おはよ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "'morning."

rows.en: “...” She turned away with a huff.

ghs.en: Touko: "...(pfuiri)"

rows.jp: シカト？

ghs.en: Ostracism?
ghs.assessment: The slang asks whether she is ignoring him. 'Ostracism' denotes broader social exclusion and changes the immediate interpersonal act.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Ignoring me?'

rows.jp: シカトですか。
rows.en: So it was the silent treatment.

ghs.en: Is this ostracism I see?
ghs.assessment: The repeated slang asks whether she is ignoring him. 'Ostracism' again substitutes a different, broader social process.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Are you ignoring me?'

rows.jp: 「パンツ……」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Wear..."
ghs.assessment: The isolated noun is 'underwear' or 'panties,' setting up the following exchange. 'Wear' is not that noun and removes the joke's concrete object.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Underwear...' or 'Panties...'

rows.jp: 「くどい」

ghs.en: Touko: "Be succint."
ghs.assessment: She calls him persistent or tiresome for repeating himself. The English orders him to be concise, changes the speech act, and misspells 'succinct.'
ghs.remedy: Use 'You're persistent' or 'Enough already.'

rows.jp: 「パンツ買ってくんない？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Please buy what I wear?"
ghs.assessment: He explicitly asks her to buy him underwear. The vague paraphrase 'what I wear' suppresses the concrete object that drives the exchange.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Won't you buy me some underwear?'

rows.jp: 「どーして私があなたのパンツを買わないといけないのっ！」
rows.en: “Why do I have to buy your underwear?!”

ghs.en: Touko: "Whyyy would I ever need to buy what you wear?!"
ghs.assessment: She explicitly protests having to buy his underwear. The vague paraphrase removes the repeated noun and weakens the comic escalation.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Why do I have to buy your underwear?'

rows.jp: 机をどついて立ちあがる冬子。
rows.en: Touko slammed the desk and stood up.

ghs.en: Touko stands, slamming fists on the desk.

rows.jp: 「朝からホットだね」
rows.en: “Hot this early in the morning, huh?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "All hott' from morning ain'tcha."

rows.jp: 親指を立てる。

ghs.en: I give her a thumbs up.
Touko: "..."

rows.jp: 冬子は親指をぐっとつかんで、ごきっと横に折った。
rows.en: Touko seized my thumb and wrenched it sideways with a crack.

ghs.en: Youko grabs my thumb tightly, and harshly twists it along with my wrist.
ghs.assessment: She grips his thumb and bends it sideways with a crack. The English turns this into twisting the thumb together with his wrist and loses the specified break-like motion.
ghs.remedy: Say that she bent his thumb sideways with a crack.

highlights.text: twists it along with my wrist

rows.jp: 「ぎえええええええっ！！」

ghs.en: Taichi: "GhyEEEEEEEH!!!"

rows.jp: 「あほーっ、折れたらどうするのだーっ！　自慰もままならないではないかーっ！」
rows.en: “You idiot! What if you’d broken it?! I wouldn’t even be able to masturbate properly!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Morooon, what if you'd broken iiit! I would never manage to console myself agaaain!"
ghs.assessment: He explicitly complains that he would not even be able to masturbate. 'Console myself' euphemizes away the sexual joke and its reason for mentioning the hand.
ghs.remedy: Use an explicit equivalent of 'I wouldn't even be able to masturbate.'

rows.jp: 危うく手首を返したからよかったものの。
rows.en: I was lucky I had managed to turn my wrist at the last second.

ghs.en: Very fortunately, she only barely managed to twist my wrist.
ghs.assessment: He says it was fortunate that he narrowly turned his wrist, which prevented worse injury. The English makes her the actor who barely managed to twist his wrist and reverses the protective causality.
ghs.remedy: Use 'It was a good thing I managed to turn my wrist in time.'

highlights.text: Very fortunately, she only barely managed to twist my wrist.

rows.jp: 「話しかけないで」

ghs.en: Touko: "Stay back and do not talk to me."
ghs.assessment: She only tells him not to talk to her. The English adds a command to keep physically away.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Don't talk to me.'

rows.jp: 「昨日のテレビ見たぁ？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Did you watch TV last night?"

rows.jp: 「話しかけないで！」

ghs.en: Touko: "Stay back and do not talk to me!"
ghs.assessment: The repeated command again concerns speaking only. The English repeats an unsupported instruction to keep physically away.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Don't talk to me!'

ghs.en: Taichi: "...mngh."

rows.jp: 話しかけないでと辛口に言われると、話しかけたくなる。
rows.en: Hearing “don’t talk to me” in that cutting voice only made me want to talk to her.

ghs.en: When I'm told in harsh tones not to approach or talk, I end up wanting to get close and talk.
ghs.assessment: Being sharply told not to speak makes him want to speak. The English twice adds physical approach and closeness that are absent from the source.
ghs.remedy: Keep both clauses about talking without adding movement or proximity.

rows.jp: 話しかけると、また、話しかけないでと辛口に言われる。
rows.en: If I did, she’d tell me not to talk to her again in the same cutting voice.

ghs.en: I get close and talk to her, but once more she harshly tells me to stay away and not to talk to her.
ghs.assessment: He talks to her and is again sharply told not to. The English adds both moving close and being ordered to stay away.
ghs.remedy: Keep the exchange about speaking without adding physical-distance commands.

highlights.text: get close and talk to her
stay away and not to talk to her

rows.jp: 話しかける
部活に行く
